note: The skills an agent needs for the code devup-mcp emits. Three origins. 'embedded' skills are DevFive's own but live in another repository: the canonical SKILL.md is vendored here so a machine with only devup-mcp installed can install them with no network, and commit/sha256 say which revision. 'own' skills are authored in this repository - there is nothing upstream to vendor from, so they carry no commit pin and refresh-skills.mjs skips them; this repository's history is their provenance. 'external' skills belong to someone else and are NOT vendored - devup-mcp reports where they come from and the command that installs them, and never runs that command itself.
documentNote: Each entry's documents[] lists every file the skill installs, by path relative to the skill directory. The same relative path is used under crates/devup-mcp/src/server/skills/<name>/ in this tree, so a document's source and its install location never disagree. A skill is single-file when that list has one SKILL.md in it.

skills.name: devup-ui
skills.title: devup-ui conventions
skills.description: Zero-runtime CSS-in-JS for React: Box/Flex/Text primitives, css()/globalCss()/keyframes(), devup.json theme tokens, responsive arrays and pseudo-selectors.
skills.usedFor: The TSX devup_figma_export returns is devup-ui code. Without this the agent does not know its components are compile-time placeholders, that $token means devup.json, or that a style prop takes a responsive array.

skills.name: devfive-frontend
skills.title: DevFive frontend conventions
skills.description: Where the generated code goes in a Next App Router project: app/ holds only layout.tsx and page.tsx, components live under components/pages/<route>/, Server Components are the default, and all styling is devup-ui props rather than an authored CSS file. Multi-file: SKILL.md plus four reference documents.
skills.usedFor: devup_figma_export returns one screen's TSX; a project is a tree of routes. This is the skill that says which file that TSX becomes and which rules it is then judged by. Without it an agent that can already write devup-ui still puts the screen in the wrong place - most visibly by switching screens with local state instead of file routing, and by authoring a .css file next to code that has globalCss().

skills.name: devup-implementation-plan
skills.title: Screen plan first, confirm once, then implement
skills.description: DevFive project intake, ERD models and supervisor work units, with the full Figma screen-plan and implementation workflow.
skills.usedFor: Without it an agent handed a Figma Section picks URLs itself and writes pages straight away, so nobody can tell afterwards which screen became which URL or whether each one works at every width. It also keeps the questions in structured rounds asked up front, instead of a trickle of prose confirmations - or a question hours into the work while nobody is at the keyboard.

skills.name: devup
skills.title: /devup: build pages or a site from Figma
skills.description: DevFive project intake, ERD models and supervisor work units, with the full Figma screen-plan and implementation workflow.
skills.usedFor: An MCP server cannot start a skill or a slash command itself. Claude Code offers this skill as /devup, and devup_skills install writes an OpenCode command beside it, so the user has one word to type that starts everything in the right order.

skills.name: changepacks
skills.title: changepacks conventions
skills.description: Version and changelog management for multi-language monorepos: when a pull request needs a changepack log, how to create one without an interactive prompt, and how .changepacks/config.json decides which paths are tracked.
skills.usedFor: Every repository devup-mcp writes into manages its versions this way. A pull request that changes a tracked path without a changepack log never moves the version, so the change reaches the base branch and is never released - and the invocation the project documents is interactive, which hangs in the shells an agent runs in. That combination is why the step gets skipped.

skills.name: vespera
skills.title: vespera conventions
skills.description: FastAPI-like DX for Rust/Axum: route handlers, Schema derivation and OpenAPI generation.
skills.usedFor: The openapi.json devup_project_context reads under scope api is generated by vespera routes.

skills.name: vespertide
skills.title: vespertide conventions
skills.description: JSON database schema definitions and migration plans: tables, columns, constraints and ENUM types.
skills.usedFor: The models/*.json devup_project_context reads under scope db are vespertide schemas.

skills.name: vercel-react-best-practices
skills.title: React/Next.js performance (Vercel Engineering)
skills.description: 40+ rules across 8 categories: eliminating waterfalls, bundle size, re-render cost, server fetching. Multi-file: SKILL.md plus an AGENTS.md and ~70 rule files.
skills.usedFor: The TSX devup_figma_export returns becomes React components; these are the performance rules they are then judged by.
skills.licenseNote: vercel-labs/agent-skills publishes no LICENSE file, so devup-mcp does not vendor or redistribute its content. It is installed from source by the agent.

skills.name: vercel-react-view-transitions
skills.title: React View Transitions (Vercel Engineering)
skills.description: React's View Transition API: <ViewTransition>, addTransitionType, CSS pseudo-elements, shared element transitions, Next.js integration. Multi-file: SKILL.md plus AGENTS.md and reference files.
skills.usedFor: Figma prototype reactions become animations; this is how to implement them with the View Transition API rather than by hand.
